Thursday, November 5, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Thursday, Nov 5, 2026

NATO is drafting deep-strike plans against Russian bases and industry if alliance territory is attacked; Brussels hosts EU and NATO talks with the US, UK, France and Germany on Ukraine security guarantees ahead of Abu Dhabi; Space Force leaders say they tracked a Russian satellite near an ICEYE commercial SAR spacecraft and warn midterm budget delays could slow Guardian growth.

← NewerFri, Nov 6, 2026All briefingsOlder →Wed, Nov 4, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: The Wall Street Journal reports NATO is building a “theory of victory” that would include conventional strikes deep inside Russia if Moscow attacks alliance territory. In Brussels, the European Commission and NATO are hosting separate working-level sessions with the United States, Ukraine, France, Germany and the UK on reconstruction and security guarantees before Nov. 10–11 talks in Abu Dhabi. And Space Force Gen. Douglas Schiess said the service tracked Russian satellite Cosmos 2612 near an ICEYE commercial SAR satellite, while warning post-election budget uncertainty could slow plans to add thousands of Guardians.

NATO

  • The Wall Street Journal reports NATO, under SACEUR Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, is developing defense plans that would strike Russian bases, supply networks and defense-industrial sites deep behind the front if Moscow attacks alliance territory, using precision missiles and cheaper drones rather than nuclear weapons; Polish Maj. Gen. Ireneusz Nowak called deep precision strike essential deterrence. (Kyiv Post)
  • Ukrainska Pravda’s read of the same WSJ reporting says alliance planners now treat border barriers alone as insufficient and want the ability to “break the warfighting system,” while Europe expands Storm Shadow/SCALP/Taurus stocks and pursues dozens of low-cost cruise-missile projects. (Ukrainska Pravda)
  • NATO and the European Commission are hosting separate Brussels sessions this week with the US, Ukraine, France, Germany, the UK and the World Bank on reconstruction and security guarantees, ahead of US-mediated Ukraine–Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11; a Coalition of the Willing exercise starts Nov. 9. (Rapporteur)
  • Ukraine’s foreign intelligence chief said the Brussels track runs Nov. 4–5, with a dedicated security-guarantees session on Thursday, and Kyiv is pressing for binding commitments—not a Budapest-style memorandum—before any settlement. (Kyiv Post)

European Union

  • The Commission adopted its 2027 work programme on Nov. 4, pledging continued Ukraine support, implementation of the EU–Ukraine Defence Industrial Pact, a new European Instrument for Strategic Enablers, and a European Security Emergency Protocol as part of a “new era for defence and security.” (European Commission)
  • Politico’s rundown of the slimmed-down 2027 agenda says Brussels is prioritizing competitiveness and economic security while still bolstering defense capabilities, with the final programme released Wednesday. (Politico Europe)
  • At the Berlin Security Conference, EU Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius warned that in purchasing-power terms Russia is set to spend nearly as much as Europe’s combined ~€500 billion next year, and urged Europeans to fill capability gaps as Washington pivots toward the Indo-Pacific. (Anadolu Agency)
  • Leonardo said nine-month orders hit €60.4 billion (+28%), boosted in part by the Iveco Defence acquisition, and highlighted GCAP, Rheinmetall and Baykar JVs, an Airbus–Thales space alliance, and Michelangelo Dome as strategic priorities. (Euronews)
  • The Commission-hosted Brussels reconstruction talks drew the US, Ukraine, France, Germany, Britain and the World Bank as a follow-on to Miami, focused on postwar prosperity and security architecture before Abu Dhabi. (UPI)

United States

  • Gen. Douglas Schiess said the Space Force and IC tracked Russian Cosmos 2612 as it maneuvered near an ICEYE commercial SAR satellite used to support Ukraine, calling it adversary messaging and reinforcing the need to defend space assets; he also said recent disclosure of US on-orbit weapons was a deliberate deterrent signal. (DefenseScoop)
  • Speaking at the Mitchell Institute, Schiess warned prolonged post-midterm budget uncertainty is already blocking new program starts and complicating plans to expand the force, even as he expects bipartisan support for the Space Force to hold. (SpaceNews)
  • Air & Space Forces Magazine’s Nov. 5 daily reports Schiess told the same forum the service wants to add about 2,800 Guardians and 2,000 civilians in FY2027 “if the budget comes through,” with much of that growth going into combatant-command components. (Air & Space Forces Magazine)
  • Former DoD space-policy chief John Plumb warned at CyberSat that branding Golden Dome around Trump, a ~$1 trillion price tag, and Democratic midterm wins could doom the branded program even as bipartisan missile defense continues. (Via Satellite)
  • Likely incoming HASC chair Adam Smith said Democrats’ top priority is vigorous Pentagon oversight—public testimony, a restored Oversight & Investigations subcommittee, Iran-war scrutiny, and a more realistic budget that does not require a $1 trillion defense topline. (House Armed Services Democrats)
  • House Select Committee on China leaders John Moolenaar and Ro Khanna pressed the Air Force for a Nov. 20 briefing on planned China Aerospace Studies Institute civilian cuts, warning under-resourcing would hurt understanding of PLA aerospace power. (Breaking Defense)
  • NASA unveiled the crewed X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft at Kennedy Space Center, a rapidly reconfigurable research platform targeting first flight within two years, Mach 0.75 cruise and ~1,500 nautical miles of range. (NASA)
  • Shield AI completed its first full-scale X-BAT VTOL autonomous strike-fighter prototype in about a year and is moving it to Newton, Kansas for engine, crane and untethered flight tests, aiming for a missionized aircraft in 2028 and production in 2029. (Air & Space Forces Magazine)
  • DARPA awarded Redwire a $20 million contract for a second very-low-Earth-orbit flight experiment expanding work on satellites that can operate for extended periods at unusually low altitudes. (SpaceNews)
  • SpaceX is still targeting Friday, Nov. 6 at 4:46 p.m. PT (backup Nov. 7) for the classified USSF-432 Falcon 9 launch from Vandenberg SLC-4E, with droneship recovery in the Pacific. (SpaceX)

European space

  • France’s DGA successfully flew ArianeGroup’s SyLEx sounding rocket from Biscarrosse overnight Nov. 3–4, its first operational exo-atmospheric mission carrying experiments for the future M51.4 SLBM less than a month after an M51 acceptance shot from SNLE Le Vigilant. (French Ministry of Armed Forces / DGA)
  • OHB won a €554 million ESA contract (with an option for a second satellite) for Sentinel-3 Next-Generation Topography, meant to replace the current Sentinel-3 topography pair with higher revisit and precision. (Aviation Week)
  • Researchers used a voice command to operate an ESA OPS-SAT PRETTY satellite on orbit for the first time—an experimental step toward satellites that can respond to distress calls at sea. (SpaceNews)

Global space & defense

  • Russia and Ukraine traded overnight drone strikes: Moscow claimed hits on a Nova Poshta hub near Kharkiv, a Dnipropetrovsk substation and a Black Sea cargo ship, while Ukrainian drones sparked fires at the Rosneft Ryazan refinery and cut power in parts of the city. (Al Jazeera)
  • China launched Ziyuan III-04 on a Long March-4B from Taiyuan, joining Ziyuan III-02/03 for high-resolution stereo mapping, natural-resource surveys and land planning—the Long March series’ 617th flight. (Space Watch Africa)
  • CAS Space’s Kinetica 2 flew its second mission from Jiuquan, placing 18 Spacesail Constellation satellites (batch 21) into orbit for China’s low-orbit satellite internet build-out. (China Daily)
